A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the intrinsic frictional properties of a range of polymers, which can be used to predict friction in a range of applications, such as in the automotive industry.
the tribological performance of a material can be predicted by the intrinsic properties of the material, such as its chemical composition and microstructure.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the intrinsic tribological behavior of polymers is a function of the polymer structure and the molecular interactions between polymer chains, and is independent of the surface roughness of the material.

the intrinsic friction of polymers is not necessarily a constant, but can be tuned by changing their chemical structure, which is a promising route for the design of novel materials with tailored tribological performance.
we have developed a simple and effective way of making polymers that can withstand frictional wear.
